Action items and next steps for on-prem dry run
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-12 16:00 PST; Duration: 58m; Attendees: Ava Martinez, Jonah Patel, Rosa Chen (Redwood) — Mira Kahn, Samir Das, Lena Ortiz, Eric Holt (Pegasus).

Summary: Short quarterly-style health check, but focused on immediate cost and reliability items. Pegasus is seeing an uptick in embedding costs tied to nightly indexing. They want a walkthrough of cost levers and plan for a two-hour private dry run.

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to do a quick check-in on usage and make sure the November anomalies are understood. Mira, Samir, do you want to kick off with what you're seeing on your side?

[00:18] Mira Kahn: Yeah, thanks Ava. Quick context — we're the search infra team for Pegasus, embedding pipelines run nightly, last two weeks we've seen token spend spike about 28% higher than forecast. The embeddings route is about 60% of the spend now. We're also seeing intermittent 95th p99 latency spikes on the inference endpoint around 2am-4am batch window.

[00:38] Samir Das: To add, we have a retention policy change that increased index granularity which may explain volume. But the latency spikes look like something else — some of the KV cache warmup isn't behaving.

[00:52] Jonah Patel: Okay that aligns with what our telemetry shows — there are a couple of correlated spikes in prefix cache misses concurrent with your batch window. Could be behavior from the KV cache invalidation during your backfill. Are you invalidating keys or is this a TTL issue?

[01:08] Mira Kahn: We rotate indexes nightly which invalidates a subset. We thought Redwood's prefix caching would absorb most of the churn, but possibly not at our scale. Also curious about quantization settings — we use 4-bit on some models in test envs, are there perf tradeoffs we should expect in Dedicated vs Private?

[01:26] Jonah Patel: Good question. Generally 4-bit quantization reduces memory footprint but can increase compute per token slightly — depends on kernel selection. In Dedicated we can tune compilers and kernel selection more aggressively, plus we can pin a quantized variant for production. In Private there is similar control but depends on your hardware and driver stack, especially for older gen GPUs.

[01:44] Lena Ortiz: From finance side — the comma here is that our committed usage is getting close to the dedicated threshold but with the spike it looks like we'll overshoot once we factor in indexing. Ava — can you run through the current committed capacity vs usage?

[01:58] Ava Martinez: Sure — quick numbers: commitment is for 2x A100-equivalent capacity (reserved pool) with a monthly token cap of roughly 1.2B generation tokens and 250M embedding tokens. Last month you consumed ~1.35B gen tokens and 320M embedding tokens (embedding delta is where the cost growth is). I'll share the month-by-month CSV after this call.

[02:16] Eric Holt: Is there a quick mitigation while we decide on Dedicated amendment? Maybe reroute embedding jobs to a cheaper model or lower precision? We need a stopgap to avoid billing surprise.

[02:31] Jonah Patel: Two immediate levers: 1) Use lower-cost embedding model for nightly index building (we can recommend models with similar vector quality at ~30-40% lower token cost), 2) Adjust batching to increase batch size during non-latency-critical windows to cut per-token overhead. We can also enable prefix caching more aggressively for your index prefix patterns.

[02:52] Samir Das: How intrusive is switching embedding model? We have eval harness and existing regressions.

[03:02] Jonah Patel: We can run a lightweight A/B — take samples from your index and score vectors with the candidate embedding; we'll produce similarity drift and topk change metrics. Low friction — do it in a day for a representative sample.

[03:18] Mira Kahn: That helps. On latency — the 2am spike seems to align with a maintenance job that touches many shards. Could Redwood's smart routing or autoscaler be throttling? We saw some 503s during one night.

[03:33] Rosa Chen: We looked at the logs for your account after the incident. There were two overlapping behaviors — a short-lived GPU reclaim during a maintenance window in the region, and your batch concurrency briefly spiked which pushed some requests to fallback model variants. Fallbacks are intended, but they can result in slightly higher tokenization overhead or different kernel paths for some architectures.

[03:56] Mira Kahn: Fallback to a different model shouldn't return 503s though.

[04:03] Jonah Patel: Correct, 503s usually indicate a transient capacity exhaustion or routing mismatch. We do have graceful degradation pipeline — but in your case the small fleet reclaim plus a concurrency burst created a race. We're proposing a policy change: reserve a minimal hot pool for your critical routes during the batch window to avoid reclaim-induced 503s. That can be part of a Dedicated amendment or configured as a hosted policy for a fee.

[04:26] Lena Ortiz: Cost tradeoffs? If we reserve a hot pool what's the incremental monthly spend?

[04:31] Ava Martinez: Rough back-of-envelope: a hot pool sufficient to cover your critical routes during the maintenance window is about 0.25 A100 equivalent, which would add roughly 8-10% to the committed capacity cost monthly but would eliminate most of the 503 events during heavy backfills. I'll model that in the pricing update.

[04:48] Eric Holt: Talk to me about timeline — we want the on-prem dry run to validate Private option. When could Redwood do a two-hour dry run and what does it require from our side?

[04:59] Rosa Chen: For an on-prem dry run we need: 1) network whitelisting of our orchestration collector (we'll provide IPs), 2) KMS integration details if you plan to bring your HSM/KMS, 3) a small set of models to exercise (embedding and one generation model). We can do a dry run next week if you can provision a test cluster and provide access.

[05:17] Mira Kahn: We can have a test cluster by 11/20. Preferred window would be 11/21-11/22 evening.

[05:23] Rosa Chen: Good — I'll target 11/21 evening and share a checklist and runbook.

[05:29] Samir Das: On security — do you provide audit log samples and do you integrate with our SIEM?

[05:36] Ava Martinez: Yes, we stream audit logs to S3 or to your SIEM via secure delivery. We'll include a sample audit log. Also we'll share the SOC 2 and ISO artifacts excerpt.

[05:45] Lena Ortiz: If we move to Dedicated or Private, how does billing change? Do we keep token billing or move to flat seat + reserved compute?

[05:53] Ava Martinez: For Dedicated we keep per-token metrics internally for cost visibility but the billing is split: reserved capacity commit fee plus a usage overage model. Private is typically an upfront license/installation fee plus either a flat monthly platform fee or a metered on-prem model depending on the customer's preference; we can craft a hybrid. I'll put sample T&Cs in the amendment.

[06:12] Eric Holt: Competitors question — we ran a side-by-side with Anthropic earlier this year; their throughput advantage was lower cost per token for embeddings but required more infra ops. How does Redwood compare?

[06:26] Jonah Patel: The difference is operational overhead. Anthropic might show lower unit cost in that benchmark but that assumes you manage the fleet and the optimizations. Redwood's value prop is the runtime + ops: the compilation and kernel selection plus smart routing and caching reduce real-world unit cost without you managing onboard optimization.

[06:41] Mira Kahn: Is there a simple way to demonstrate that with our workload?

[06:46] Jonah Patel: Yes — Jonah: run the 10k token benchmark with your indexing trace on Redwood Hosted vs a comparable self-hosted baseline. We'll instrument and show per-token cost and 95th latency. We'll run that for you and share the spreadsheet.

[06:58] Ava Martinez: Okay let's recap next steps and owners — Rosa will send SOC2 excerpt and runbook; Jonah will run perf benchmark; I'll update pricing and send commitment amendment; Mira will confirm on-prem window. Anything else?

[07:12] Mira Kahn: Please also include a recommended lower-cost embedding variant and a short evaluation report.

[07:17] Jonah Patel: We'll include the candidate model and delta metrics (top-k recall, vector drift) in the report.

[07:23] Lena Ortiz: Finance asking for invoice timing if we change commitment mid-month — can we prorate?

[07:28] Ava Martinez: Yes proration is standard when changing commitment mid-cycle. I'll note that in the amendment.

[07:34] Eric Holt: Last question — data residency for some of our European records. If we go Private, can we ensure European KMS and no egress?

[07:44] Rosa Chen: Yes, Private supports regional KMS and an air-gapped deployment if needed. We'll include options in the runbook.

[07:52] Mira Kahn: Thanks everyone — this was great. We'll look to confirm the 11/21 window and expect the docs from Redwood.

[07:58] Ava Martinez: Thanks all. Rosa/Jonah/Ava will follow up with the artifacts.

[08:04] (end)

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (K V cache vs KV cache), some speaker attribution simplified (roles appended). Recorded meeting length matches duration ~58 min (timestamps are approximate).
